text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- The Senate approved the bill on bank privatisation.
- The government plans to discuss amendments to the bill on foreign investments next week.
- Romania's mushroom exporters are affected by red tape and high taxes, the paper says.
- The Black Sea port of Constanta was closed due to strong gales.
- Police found 1.5 million forged cigarette stamps.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The number of foreign tourists visiting Romania is on the slide, the paper says.
- The Phoenix SA copper smelter in Baia Mare has some 1,000 tonnes of copper in stock.
- The distribution of credits to the farming sector proceeds at a slow pace, the paper says.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Romania has turned for some big foreign companies into a paradise for alleged illegal businesses, the paper says, quoting a report by the Court of accounts.
- River traffic on the Danube was affected by strong winds.
- The bill on leasing farmland will be discussed by parliament in emergency procedure.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Five state banks will be privatised under the new bill on bank privatisation, the paper says.
- Foreign investments rose by 35 percent in the first quarter of 1997.
- Losses in the mining sector amounted to 620 billion lei last year, the paper says.
- The cargo ship Arad ran aground near the Russian port of Novorossisk.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Cold weather destroyed 60 percent of this year's apricot crop.
- Ruling National Peasant Party (PNT-CD) vice-president Gabriel Tepelea will run for the presidency of the European Christian-Democratic Union, PNT-CD leader Ion Diaconescu said.

- Romania's King Michael held a speach at the Clingendoel Royal Institute for International Studies in The Hague to plead for his country's early admission into NATO. He is expected to meet Netherlands' Queen Beatrix on Tuesday.
ADEVARUL
- One person died and two others were seriously wounded in an explosion caused by a gas leak in a Bucharest block of flats.
- President Emil Constantinescu met opposition leaders to discuss their support for the government's reform package.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Leaders of the Romanian Orthodox Church called for a reconciliation with the Greek-Catholic Church in Transylvania and pledged to help them build village churches.

- Transport Minister Traian Basescu asked his ministry's employees to give their personal opinion on Romania's integration into NATO and the EU and on ministry policies. Basescu said he wanted to test his employees' understanding of the reform.
- King Michael will spend Orthodox Easter at Timisoara. His visit starts on April 25 and ends on May 7.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Italian Interior Minister Giorgio Napolitano starts visit to Romania to boost bilateral cooperation on fighting smuggling and illegal immigration.
- Labour Minister Alexandru Athanasiu said the monthly allowance for children could be increased to 100,000 lei, from the present 50,000. ($= 7,051lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
